ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a four-variable Karnaugh map. The row label is AB, arranged in Gray code order as 00, 01, 11, 10; the column label is CD, arranged in Gray code order as 00, 01, 11, 10. The 1s in the figure are distributed as: the four corner cells are 1, namely AB=00/CD=00, AB=00/CD=10, AB=10/CD=00, AB=10/CD=10; there is a 2×2 block of 1s in the middle, namely the intersection cells of rows AB=01, 11 and columns CD=01, 11. Reasoning: First combine the 1s at the four corners into one group by using the wraparound adjacency of the K-map. In this group, A and C vary, while B=0 and D=0 remain unchanged, so the term B'D' is obtained. Then combine the four 1s in the middle 2×2 into one group. In this group, A and C vary, while B=1 and D=1 remain unchanged, so the term BD is obtained. OR the two product terms to obtain the simplest sum-of-products expression F = BD + B'D'.
